# Pipeline pressure protection

`process.pipeline_pressure_protection`

## Source

**NeqSim process/safety/overpressure/PipelinePressureProtectionCalculator.java**

Its `calcProtection`, `getMaxIncidentalPressure`, `getDesignMargin` and the three verdict getters.


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `closed_form_pipeline_pressure_protection` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-12` |
| Max iterations | `1` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `max_source_pressure` | bar | the maximum credible source pressure, above zero. |
| `design_pressure` | bar | the segment design pressure, above zero. |
| `incidental_factor` | dimensionless | the incidental factor, at least one; typically 1.1. |
| `barrier1_setpoint` | bar | the first barrier's set point, above zero. |
| `barrier2_setpoint` | bar | the second barrier's set point, above zero. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `max_incidental_pressure` | bar | `incidental_factor design_pressure`. |
| `design_margin` | bar | `design_pressure - max_source_pressure`, negative when under-rated. |
| `fully_rated` | - | whether the maximum source pressure is at or below the design pressure. |
| `barrier1_adequate` | - | whether barrier 1's set point is at or below the design pressure. |
| `barrier2_adequate` | - | whether barrier 2's set point is at or below the maximum incidental pressure. |
| `protection_adequate` | - | whether the segment is fully rated or both barriers are adequate. |
| `verdict` | - | `FULLY_RATED`, `TWO_BARRIERS_REQUIRED` or `INSUFFICIENT`, the class's own spellings. |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `max_source_pressure > 0` | raises | the class accepts a non-positive source pressure; it is not a pressure |
| `design_pressure > 0` | raises | the class accepts a non-positive design pressure; it is not a pressure |
| `incidental_factor >= 1` | raises | the class's javadoc calls for at least one and its setter does not check |
| `barrier1_setpoint > 0` | raises | the class accepts a non-positive set point; it is not a pressure |
| `barrier2_setpoint > 0` | raises | the class accepts a non-positive set point; it is not a pressure |

## Assumptions

- **the maximum incidental pressure is `incidental_factor design_pressure`**, and the design margin is `design_pressure - max_source_pressure`.
- **the segment is fully rated when the maximum source pressure is at or below the design pressure.**
- **barrier 1 is adequate when its set point is at or below the design pressure**, and barrier 2 when it is at or below the maximum incidental pressure.
- **protection is adequate when the segment is fully rated or both barriers are adequate**; the verdict is fully-rated first, then two barriers, else insufficient.
- **the class validates nothing**: its setters accept non-positive pressures and a factor below one. The port refuses both.

## How far this is checked
**`partially_verified`** — exercised against expectations pinned in its own spec, with no independent oracle recorded for it - **the normal case rather than a defect**.

- Tests: 6 declared, every one run
- External check: no external validation case names it
